newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt, futures down with eye on U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: German debt, futures down with eye on U.S. market.

text.p: German Bunds and futures traded at lower levels in late dealings on Wednesday but off the day's heaviest losses linked to disappointment about the quick reversal of gains in U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday.
At 1600 GMT, DTB March Bund futures were down 39 basis points at 101.01 points but well off the low at 100.84 reached briefly after the release of U.S. durable goods data.
The 10-year cash Bund due January 2007 was at 101.35 and yielded 5.81 percent, down from Tuesday's close at 101.71.
"The U.S. market is driving us since there is otherwise not much to report about the German market," said one trader.
Traders said the market's gyrations has led to diverse opinions about the near-term market direction.

Some market participants are looking for a correction toward 99.00 in the near-term, while others look for prices to remain steady in a consolidative mode and for the futures contract to trade between 100.70 and 101.50 points.

In the meantime, traders said the focus will be on the U.S. credit market, which gyrated in volatile dealings after December durable goods dropped an unexpected 1.7 percent, and on Thursday's weekly jobless claims report at 1330 GMT.
